gaps.sentence: If she ___ the warning signs, the accident would not have happened.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had noticed.

gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: We will lose the deposit if we ___ the booking now.
gaps.explanation: The result clause carries 'will'; the if-clause stays in the present simple: cancel.

gaps.sentence: If he had not left his passport at home, he ___ the earlier flight.
gaps.hint: third conditional result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The unreal past result takes 'would have' plus the participle: would have caught.

gaps.sentence: If the alarm sounds, ___ the building immediately.
gaps.hint: an instruction after if, imperative result
gaps.explanation: Instructions after 'if' keep the present simple in the if-clause and use the imperative as the result: leave.

gaps.sentence: ___ there be any problems, call this number.
I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.
